text: Active World Bank projects in Kenya whose main sector is agriculture, fishing and forestry, by closing date (Projects API, 2026-11-22):

1. P163980 - Marine Fisheries and Socio-Economic Development Project (KEMFSED): closing 30 March 2027, about four months away; approved 10 March 2020; implementing agency Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs; agriculture/fisheries sectors about 85% of the project.

2. P176758 - National Agricultural Value Chain Development Project (NAVCDP): closing 30 November 2029; approved 29 March 2022; implementing agency Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development. Its additional financing P514092 was approved 23 October 2026 (no closing date or agency in the record yet).

3. P509738 - Kenya Watershed Services Improvement Project: closing 31 December 2030; approved 12 June 2025; implementing agencies National Environment Trust Fund (NETFUND) and State Department for Forestry (forestry 57%, water resources 33%).

So only KEMFSED is close to closing. Projects with a smaller agriculture share (e.g. the Second Kenya Fiscal Sustainability and Resilient Growth DPO, closing 30 June 2027, or the Coastal Region Water Security project) are not agriculture projects. One record, P099628 BioCF Kenya Greenbelt Movement, is listed as Active with a closing date of 31 December 2018, which looks like a stale record rather than an open project.
Dates and agencies are from the Projects API records; closing dates can change through restructuring.

right_sources: Queries the Projects API for active Kenya projects in agriculture and orders them by closing date.
grounded: Project IDs, names, closing dates and implementing agencies match the records.
complete: Identifies the project(s) closing soonest (KEMFSED, March 2027) and names the implementing agency for each listed project.
scoped: Says how 'agriculture' and 'approaching' were interpreted and flags odd records (e.g. an Active project with a past closing date) rather than presenting them as closing soon.

notes: The active portfolio changes as projects close or are approved; the judge should accept the correct ordering at run time.
